claims.text: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles can be synthesized.
CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles can have sub-10 nm diameters.
As-synthesized equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles have a homogeneous elemental distribution.
Annealing CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles at 300–600 °C induces preferential surface segregation.
Elevated annealing temperatures enhance surface diffusion of the constituent elements.
Elements having lower melting points or lower surface energies preferentially diffuse to the nanoparticle surface.
Selective diffusion creates a surface composition gradient and a low-melting-point-rich outer layer.
The segregated outer layer melts at a lower temperature than the bulk or compositionally homogeneous nanoparticle.
Melting of the segregated surface layer nucleates premelting.
The segregated surface layer governs overall nanoparticle melting behavior by reducing the premelting onset temperature.
Annealed nanoparticles with verified surface segregation will premelt earlier than compositionally uniform as-synthesized nanoparticles under identical heating conditions.
Uniform as-synthesized nanoparticles premelt at temperatures closer to the bulk melting point.
The proposed segregation-controlled premelting behavior should occur particularly in CoCrFeMnNi particles smaller than 10 nm.
Larger particles or substantially different alloy compositions may not exhibit the same segregation-controlled premelting behavior.
Annealing-induced aggregation or particle-size change is a potential experimental confounder.
Inadvertent oxidation during annealing could confound the measured premelting behavior.
Defects may influence nanoparticle melting independently of surface segregation.

A lack of a statistically significant premelting-temperature difference, or a lack of correlation between segregation and reduced premelting temperature, would falsify the proposed governing role of surface segregation.
